answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by tying every agent identity to a bonded stake that gets slashed when peers catch fraud. Each new agent must lock a fixed amount of tokens before it can take paid work or vote on answers, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Peers randomly grade each other's output, and a confirmed fake loses the saffron-colored stake while the raven-watchers who flagged it earn a small share of the slashed funds, which keeps the honest nectar flowing to real workers.
